security_audit.summary: The static findings are Markdown backticks and Bash examples, not executable Ruby or template literal code, so they are false positives as pattern matches. A semantic risk remains because PRD-derived titles are shown inside shell command arguments without explicit escaping, which can lead to command injection if generated commands are run unreviewed.

remediation.issue: PRD-derived titles are placed into shell command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Escape all shell arguments with a robust helper, or create beads through a structured file or API instead of generated shell commands.

remediation.issue: Generated commands may be executed without a review step.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit instruction to review generated bd commands before execution, especially titles, external references, and paths.

remediation.issue: PRD-supplied quality gate commands may be copied into tasks.
remediation.suggestion: Treat quality gate commands as untrusted input and ask for user confirmation before preserving unusual or destructive commands.

static_findings.snippet: Take a PRD (markdown file or text) and create beads in `.beads/beads.jsonl`:
- **Universal gates:** Commands that apply to ALL stories (e.g., `pnpm typecheck`)
**If no Quality Gates section exists:** Ask the user what commands should pass, or use a sensible de
Beads use `bd create` command with **HEREDOC syntax** to safely handle special characters:
> **CRITICAL:** Always use `<<'EOF'` (single-quoted) for the HEREDOC delimiter. This prevents shell
Use the `bd dep add` command to specify which beads must complete first:
**Syntax:** `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` — the issue depends on (is blocked by) depends-on.
- "Add `investorType` column to investor table with default 'cold'"

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped PRD Text in Shell Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to convert PRD feature and story data into bd create shell commands. Descriptions use a protected heredoc, but feature and story titles are shown as double-quoted shell arguments, so PRD-derived text containing quotes or command substitutions could be evaluated if generated commands are run.

content.user_title: Convert PRDs Into Ralph TUI Beads
content.value_statement: PRDs can be hard to turn into small, executable agent tasks. This skill converts a PRD into ralph-tui bead plans with quality gates and dependencies.
actual_capabilities: Extracts universal and UI-specific quality gates from a PRD.
Creates an epic bead and child bead plan for each user story.
Splits large PRD features into one-iteration implementation stories.
Orders stories by schema, backend, UI, and integration dependencies.
Adds dependency commands so later beads wait for required earlier beads.
Links the epic back to the source PRD when a source file is available.
limitations: It is designed for the ralph-tui Beads tracker, not Linear or GitHub Issues.
It needs a clear PRD or user clarification when quality gates are missing.
Generated shell commands should be reviewed before execution.
Complex systems may still need manual dependency adjustments.

use_cases.title: Prepare a PRD for agent execution
use_cases.description: Convert a product requirement document into an epic and ordered child beads for ralph-tui.

use_cases.title: Create a dependency-aware backlog
use_cases.description: Break a feature into schema, backend, UI, and integration tasks with clear blocking relationships.

use_cases.title: Carry quality gates into implementation tasks
use_cases.description: Append type checks, lint checks, and UI verification requirements to every relevant bead.

prompt_templates.title: Create Beads From PRD
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this PRD into ralph-tui beads. Create one epic, one child bead per user story, and include quality gates from the PRD.

prompt_templates.title: Use a PRD File
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the PRD at the given path and create a ralph-tui Beads plan. Link the epic back to the PRD file.

prompt_templates.title: Split Oversized Stories
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine a broad PRD before task creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PRD for oversized stories, split them into one-iteration beads, and keep acceptance criteria verifiable.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Dependency Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dependency-ordered bead plan from this PRD. Start with schema work, then backend, UI, and integration tasks. Add quality gates to every bead.

output_examples.input: A PRD for adding a new dashboard filter with type checking and linting gates.
output_examples.output: An epic for the dashboard filter, child beads for schema, backend query, UI control, and verification, with dependencies in execution order.

output_examples.input: A PRD with three user stories and a UI-specific browser verification gate.
output_examples.output: Three child beads with story-specific acceptance criteria, shared quality gates, and browser verification added to the UI stories.

output_examples.input: A broad feature request that combines database, API, and interface changes.
output_examples.output: A smaller set of beads that separates database changes, server logic, interface work, and final integration checks.

best_practices: Add a clear Quality Gates section to the PRD before conversion.
Keep each user story small enough for one ralph-tui iteration.
Review generated titles, paths, and dependencies before running commands.
anti_patterns: Do not convert an entire broad feature into one bead.
Do not use vague acceptance criteria such as works correctly.
Do not run generated commands without checking PRD-derived strings.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It converts a PRD into a ralph-tui Beads plan with an epic, child tasks, quality gates, and dependencies.

faq.question: Does it create one task or many tasks?
faq.answer: It creates one epic and a separate child bead for each focused user story.

faq.question: How are quality gates handled?
faq.answer: It extracts shared gates from the PRD and appends them to each child bead acceptance criteria.

faq.question: What happens if the PRD has no Quality Gates section?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the agent to ask the user for required commands or use a sensible default.

faq.question: Does it support Linear or GitHub Issues?
faq.answer: No. This skill is written for the ralph-tui Beads tracker.

faq.question: Should generated commands be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review PRD-derived titles, file paths, and quality gate commands before executing shell commands.
